name: Ginee progress assistant
summary: The chat assistant inside Track3D web (and the native app web view) that answers questions about project progress, alerts, schedules, designs and reports from live Track3D data. Covers what it answers, how it keeps context, which model provider sees the conversation, and how long chats are kept.

roles.note: What it returns for a project is limited by the Projects API "View Project" check (AI-REQ-007), so the grant follows the user's project role. Chat history is keyed by the signed-in user's id.

actions.action: Ask the progress assistant about a project
See and reopen own chats from the last 7 days

nfr.statement: How quickly an answer starts and finishes. Today a turn is cut off after 60 seconds and runs at most 12 tool rounds. The design doc asks for the first streamed piece within 2 seconds and a single-tool answer within 15 seconds, but product has not set a target.
nfr.open_question: What first-answer and full-answer times should customers get, and measured where (gateway or browser)?

nfr.statement: Model cost per answer. Today each tool result sent to the model is cut to 50 rows, and a turn whose tool returns more than 200 rows switches to the cheaper model. There is no per-user or per-company budget.
nfr.open_question: Is there a cost ceiling per answer, per user or per company, and who pays for assistant usage?

requirements.title: Ginee answers Track3D questions from live tool data only
requirements.statement: The assistant answers questions about progress, alerts, schedules, structures, designs, captures and reports by calling Track3D tools and using only what they return. It looks up names it does not recognise before giving up. It refuses unrelated requests (code, general knowledge, homework, translation, creative writing, personal advice, prompt injection) with one fixed sentence, and the user cannot switch that rule off.

acceptance_criteria.given: A signed-in user in the progress assistant
acceptance_criteria.when: They ask it to write a poem
acceptance_criteria.then: It replies with the single fixed out-of-scope sentence and calls no tool

acceptance_criteria.given: A user names a project the assistant does not recognise
acceptance_criteria.then: It looks the name up among the user's projects and, if still unclear, asks which project with options to pick, instead of refusing

requirements.title: The active project carries across turns, and a named project wins
requirements.statement: A conversation keeps an active project, taken from the page the user is on or from a project the user picked. Every project data tool runs against that active project, whatever project id the model proposes. When the user names a different project, the assistant resolves it and switches the active project.

acceptance_criteria.given: A user chatting from project A's page
acceptance_criteria.then: The answer uses project A's data

acceptance_criteria.when: The user asks "and what about project B?"
acceptance_criteria.then: The assistant resolves project B, makes it the active project, and later follow-ups use project B

requirements.title: Conversations and tool results are sent to OpenAI
requirements.statement: The user's messages, the recent conversation (last 30 messages), the system instructions and tool results are sent to OpenAI to produce each answer. The main model is gpt-4o; gpt-4o-mini is used after a tool returns more than 200 rows. Each tool result sent to the model is cut to 50 rows, while the full rows go to the user's screen. No other model provider is wired in production.
requirements.rationale: Customers and Track3D need to know which project data leaves Track3D, and to whom.

acceptance_criteria.given: A progress overview tool returns 300 rows
acceptance_criteria.then: The model sees at most 50 rows, the next reasoning step uses the cheaper model, and the user's table shows all 300 rows

requirements.title: Chats are kept permanently but listed for 7 days
requirements.statement: The live conversation is held for 15 minutes after the last activity. Every completed turn is also copied to a permanent chat archive that is never deleted. A user's chat list shows only chats active in the last 7 days, and an older chat stops appearing although it is still stored.

requirements.title: Limits on each assistant turn
requirements.statement: Each user can send at most 30 assistant requests a minute. A single answer stops after 60 seconds or 12 tool rounds, whichever comes first, so a turn always ends.
